Thanks Jared/Sofia 

good call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Integration surface: JavaScript SDK + server-side Python client for embedding / reranking + streaming chat for a subset of product flows.
- Auth: API key for server-to-server; short-lived tokens + KMS integration for higher-security flows.
- Routing: prefer regional routing (us-east for production) with automatic fallback to hosted multi-region.
- Rate limiting/quotas: you likely need per-minute request quotas for embedding jobs and token-based quotas for generation.
- Retries/idempotency: 429 handling, exponential backoff, and Idempotency-Key for write-like ops.

Action items / next steps:
1) I attached the Redwood SDK integration guide and a sample embedding workflow spreadsheet. Review and share with your infra folks. (See attachments)
2) Can you send us an estimate of embedding request volume (requests/min) and typical sequence length? That’ll help us size a dedicated quota for the pilot.
3) We’ll provide a recommended client-side retry pattern + server-side rate limit headers for your engineers.
4) Marissa will follow up with a trial quota bump and a test API key for your staging environment.

A note on expected behavior (technical):
- For embeddings/rerank, we recommend batching small requests (<=32 vectors per batch) and using a per-request X-Request-ID header.
- On 429s, client should use standard exponential backoff with jitter. We include Retry-After when possible; when absent, start at 500ms and double (max 8s).
- For idempotency in generation requests (if you call function/tool outputs that change external state), include Idempotency-Key and treat non-2xx as retryable only if the server returns an explicit failure that is safe to re-run.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf, acme-embedding-workflow.xlsx

Thanks Jared — great questions. Passing along a concise recommendation your engineers can implement quickly. Short answers first, details after: 

Short answers:
- Embeddings: start with a dedicated quota for the pilot (we can flex up). 120 req/min is fine with batching; recommend provisioning for 200 req/min to allow headroom.
- Observability: include X-Request-ID and Idempotency-Key in every call; log both client- and server-returned request_id values.
- Reranking in-path: prefer fast-fail with a graceful degrade (fallback to cached scores) on 429s for user-facing low-latency paths, and async retry for background / non-latency-critical flows.

Technical recommendation (copy/paste for your infra doc):
- Headers we return / accept:
  - X-Request-ID: a UUIDv4 generated by the client. Reduces ambiguity in logs.
  - Idempotency-Key: for idempotent operations that may mutate state (string, up to 128 chars).
  - Retry-After: standard HTTP header when we issue a rate-limit window (seconds).
  - X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset: per-route quota hints.

- Client retry policy (recommended):
  1) On 429: if Retry-After provided -> wait that many seconds.
  2) If no Retry-After: use exponential backoff with full jitter. Start=500ms, max=8000ms. Max attempts = 5.
  3) For idempotent embedding/rerank calls: safe to retry automatically. For generation calls that may affect state (e.g., tool calls), only retry if Idempotency-Key is present.

- Batching / concurrency:
  - For embeddings: batch up to 32 vectors or ~4k tokens per request. For your 120 req/min estimate, we recommend client-side batching to reduce RPS.
  - For rerank (sync): use a low concurrency pool (e.g., 8 concurrent requests per node) and fall back to cached results on 429s to keep p99 latency bounded.

- Server-side: we'll enable per-route quotas for your project and set an initial per-minute quota of 200 embedding requests and a generation token quota aligned with your forecast. We will also enable the headers above so your observability can reconcile requests.

I'll have Marissa open a trial quota request and a test API key for staging. Attaching a brief snippet your engineers can paste into their client logs: 

[LOG EXAMPLE]
RequestID=%s IdempotencyKey=%s Endpoint=/v1/embeddings Status=429 RetryAfter=3

If helpful, we can do a short 30-min tech session next week to walk through SDK examples and run some load tests.
